title: Planned Repair Days at Authorization — Insurance Claim Repairs Planning Office Rule
content:
**Rule.** When the insurer's authorization of the original estimate is recorded, an Insurance Claim Repairs repair order moves to authorized and its planned repair days are fixed. The plan takes the estimated labor hours on the repair order, adds the labor hours of every signed customer-pay addition consent on the repair order, divides that total by the class's labor hours per production day, rounds the quotient up to the next whole day and adds the class's intake and delivery days.

The two class figures — labor hours per production day and intake and delivery days — are those of the repair order's class in the Insurance Claim Repairs production planning rates.

## The plan, line by line

1. **Planned hours** — the estimated labor hours on the repair order, together with the labor hours of every signed customer-pay addition consent on it.
2. **Production days** — the planned hours divided by the class's labor hours per production day, rounded up to the next whole day. A quotient that is already a whole number stays as it is; any fraction of a day, however small, makes a further whole day.
3. **Planned repair days** — the production days plus the class's intake and delivery days.

The planned repair days are a whole number of days.

## Worked plans (hypothetical repair orders)

**A class with 5.0 labor hours per production day and 1 intake and delivery day; 23.4 estimated labor hours; one signed customer-pay addition consent of 3.0 hours.**
- Planned hours: 23.4 and 3.0, 26.4 hours.
- 26.4 divided by 5.0 is 5.28; rounded up, 6 production days.
- Planned repair days: 6 and 1, **7**.

**The same class; 20.0 estimated labor hours; no signed customer-pay addition consent.**
- 20.0 divided by 5.0 is exactly 4; 4 production days.
- Planned repair days: **5**.

**A class with 4.5 labor hours per production day and 2 intake and delivery days; 18.2 estimated labor hours; no signed customer-pay addition consent.**
- 18.2 divided by 4.5 is 4.04; rounded up, 5 production days.
- Planned repair days: **7**.

## Basis Q&A

**Which customer-pay hours enter the plan?** The labor hours of the customer-pay addition consents on the repair order that are signed.

**Is the rounding to the nearest day?** No. The quotient is rounded up: 4.04 becomes 5.
